title: Co-founder pitch and agreement checklist
intro: A one-page pitch for someone you'd like to start a company with: what you've learned, what you need and what's still uncertain, plus the topics you'll agree on in writing before anyone commits. It's a starting point for a conversation, not a legal agreement.

fields.label: Company or project name
fields.help: A working name is fine, such as 'Home-care scheduling'.

fields.label: The problem, in one line
fields.help: Say it the way a customer would, without mentioning your product, such as 'Coordinators lose hours rebuilding the visit schedule whenever a carer calls in sick.'
fields.placeholder: e.g. Coordinators lose hours rebuilding the schedule whenever a carer calls in sick.

fields.label: What you've learned so far
fields.help: Evidence rather than opinions, such as '12 interviews; 9 rebuild the schedule by hand every week; 2 asked to try a prototype.'

fields.label: The role you need filled
fields.help: What this person would own and achieve in the first six months, not just a title, such as 'Own the product and build the first version.'

fields.label: What you bring
fields.help: Your skills, experience, contacts, time and any money you can put in, described as honestly as the role, such as 'Eight years managing a care agency and 40 coordinators who will take my call.'

fields.label: Time commitment expected
fields.help: Hours per week and dates for both of you, such as 'About 15 hours a week each until March, then full-time if we have five paying customers.'

fields.label: How decisions will be made
fields.help: Who decides what alone, what needs both of you and how you'll break a deadlock, such as 'Each of us decides within our own area; spending above an agreed amount needs both of us; check-in every Monday.'

fields.label: Topics to agree in writing
fields.help: One topic per line, such as roles, decision-making, time, money, equity split, vesting, ownership of work and what happens if someone leaves.

fields.label: First project to do together
fields.help: Real work with a clear finish in two to six weeks, such as 'Interview ten coordinators together and write up what we learned by 30 January.'

fields.label: Date to decide
fields.help: A date shortly after the project ends, when each of you will say yes or no.
